_comment: The rows of the side-by-side table, in order. 'plain' is the label in Plain mode, 'help' its one-line meaning; 'detail_only' rows show only in Detail mode. 'flag' rows hold yes / no / some / later.

rows.label: Member price, pair
rows.help: Costco member price for a pair with the charger. Prices vary by state and change often.

rows.label: Member price, single
rows.help: For one ear only.

rows.label: Brand (parent group)
rows.help: The brand on the box and the hearing aid company behind it.

rows.label: Closest clinic model
rows.help: The more expensive model sold in private clinics that shares its technology. Features and software can differ.

rows.label: Platform / chip
rows.help: The chip and processing platform.

rows.label: At Costco since
rows.help: When it first appeared in Costco hearing aid centres.

rows.label: Styles
rows.help: RIC: a small case behind the ear with a thin wire to a speaker in the canal. In-the-canal: a custom shell that sits in the ear.

rows.label: Receivers (max output)
rows.help: Stronger speakers (receivers) fit greater hearing loss.

rows.label: Fitting range
rows.help: The degrees of hearing loss the aid can be set up for. Your hearing test decides.

rows.label: IP68 dust and water
rows.help: IP68 means sealed against dust and resistant to water. Still take them off to shower or swim.

rows.label: Colours
rows.help: Shell colours offered.

rows.label: Rechargeable
rows.help: Charges overnight in a case, like a phone. No tiny batteries to change.

rows.label: Hours per charge
rows.help: Maker's figures. Streaming and noise programs use more power.

rows.label: Charge time
rows.help: Time to a full charge, and what a quick top-up gives you.

rows.label: Disposable battery option
rows.help: Some styles use small zinc-air batteries you replace every few days.

rows.label: iPhone streaming (MFi / LE Audio)
rows.help: Phone calls, music and videos from an iPhone play straight into the aids.

rows.label: Android streaming (ASHA / LE Audio / Classic)
rows.help: Calls and audio from Android phones play straight into the aids. Depends on the phone model.

rows.label: Bluetooth stack
rows.help: The wireless standards it speaks.

rows.label: Auracast broadcast audio
rows.help: A new kind of public broadcast (airports, gyms, TVs) the aids can tune into, like a radio station.

rows.label: Hands-free calls
rows.help: Talk on the phone with the phone in your pocket: the aids' microphones pick up your voice.

rows.label: Telecoil
rows.help: Picks up hearing loops in theatres, churches and ticket windows.

rows.label: Tap control
rows.help: Double-tap your ear to answer a call or pause music.

rows.label: Channels / bands
rows.help: How finely the sound is split up for tuning. More is not always better.

rows.label: Noise and speech features
rows.help: How it helps you follow speech in restaurants and crowds.

rows.label: AI / DNN processing
rows.help: Uses a trained neural network to separate speech from noise or pick settings.

rows.label: Motion sensor
rows.help: Senses movement to change how it focuses: ahead when still, around you when walking.

rows.label: Tinnitus sound program
rows.help: Plays soft sounds to ease ringing in the ears. Costco's fitting software may not turn this on.

rows.label: CROS / BiCROS option
rows.help: For one ear that an aid cannot help: a mic on that side sends sound to the better ear.

rows.label: User app
rows.help: The app for volume, programs and battery.

rows.label: Remote care
rows.help: Your hearing aid specialist can fine-tune the aids over the internet.
